content.title: About
content.content: Corn nuts are roasted whole corn kernels that become crunchy and lightly salted after processing. They have a distinctive roasted‑corn aroma and a dense texture that resembles nuts, although botanically they are not nuts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn nuts were introduced in the United States in the 1930s as a cinema snack.
To achieve their crunch, the kernels are first soaked and then deep‑fried at high temperature.
Several flavor variants exist: classic salted, barbecue, cheese, spicy chili, and more.
The corn used is often a small‑kernel variety (similar to popcorn), but the grains are dried and fried rather than popped.
In some countries they are called “roasted corn” or “corn chips shaped like nuts.”

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Corn nuts provide fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Corn contains carotenoids and phenolic compounds with antioxidant activity.

items.title: Low sodium (unsalted version)
items.content: Unsalted corn nuts can be a better alternative to heavily salted snacks.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: The carbohydrates in corn are rapidly digestible, making the snack convenient for active people.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Corn is naturally gluten‑free, so corn nuts are suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn, ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salted varieties can contain a lot of sodium, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Corn nuts are relatively calorie‑dense, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: The hard texture can pose a choking risk for young children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn nuts can be enjoyed straight from the bag, added to salads, soups, or used as a crunchy topping for yogurts and porridge. They are also commonly served with dips such as cheese or spicy sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep corn nuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.
